title: microrelease-orchestration-playbook-for-llm-decoupling-wip
content:
Purpose:
Quick, operational playbook for running microreleases that decouple model and routing changes for latency-sensitive LLM endpoints. Focus: reduce blast radius for small-scope LLM changes (prompt templates, reranker weighting, quantization knobs, KV cache policies) while enabling rapid iteration across product + infra teams.

Context / problem:
- Many rollouts today bundle model change + routing + frontend changes and cause correlated failures (latency spikes + behavioral drift) that are expensive to triage.
- We need a repeatable choreography and small-phase experiments so teams can ship small steps and observe independent signals.
- Playback: this doc is an ops-first sketch (runbook + checklist + quick simulation notes) intended for cross-functional run-theatre.

Scope (what this playbook covers):
- Microrelease definition (<=5% traffic slice, single logical change)
- Decoupling tactics: separate model artifact, routing policy, and telemetry exposure steps
- Staging choreography: dev -> canary -> pilot -> gradual -> full
- Clear signal definitions and rollback triggers
- Lightweight simulation and synthetic traffic recipes

Principles:
1) Minimize simultaneous variables (change one axis at a time: model OR routing OR prompt)
2) Fast observable feedback (instrument token-level latency, tail p99, top-N behavioral deltas)
3) Human-in-loop early (steward assigned for first 48h after slice expansion)
4) Safety-first defaults (auto rollback thresholds conservative)

Actors & roles:
- Release Owner (product/PM): owns hypothesis, rollout window, comms
- Steward (oncall SRE/Owner): owns immediate rollback and runbook execution
- Eval Lead (ML/Applied ML): defines prompt sets, evaluation harness, quality thresholds
- Traffic Operator (Console team): configures slices, routing policies, rate limits
- Observability Lead: details dashboards and alert tuning

Microrelease flow (detailed):
1) Preflight (local + staging): smoke tests, eval harness pass, perf regression < 2% tokens cost delta, latency regression < 5ms median
   - Link to checklist: JIRA-PLAT-8891 checklist items 1-6.
2) Dry canary (0.1% synthetic traffic in staging region): run synthetic probe set (10k queries) for 2h. Confirm no functional regressions and stable KV/memory growth.
3) Small canary (1% production traffic): steward monitors p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, model divergence score from eval suite. Keep at 1% for 6h or until 2000 real queries.
4) Pilot cohort (5% targeted cohort): run for 24h with human review of top failure cases and drift biopsies.
5) Gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 50%): each step min 12h and requires greenlight from Steward + Observability Lead.
6) Full release (100%): post-mortem and retro cadence scheduled within 3 business days.

Decoupling patterns (examples):
- Model-only microrelease: change model artifact but keep routing weights and fallback rules constant. If latency regresses, rollback model without touching routing.
- Routing-only microrelease: change slice allocation or fallback tiering to test hybrid-cost routing. If quality drops, revert routing.
- Prompt/Template-only microrelease: update prompt templates for a cohort; regression measured by evaluation harness.

Gating matrix (key signals and thresholds):
- Safety/quality: evaluation harness pass rate drop > 1.5% OR critical intent failure increase > 0.5% => BLOCK/ROLLBACK
- Latency: p99 increase > 20% OR absolute p99 > 800ms => PAUSE and scale investigation
- Errors: 5xx rate increase > 3x baseline OR new error spike > 0.5% of slice => ROLLBACK
- Cost: per-token cost increase > 15% without commensurate quality improvement => INVESTIGATE (may pause ramp)
- Behavioral drift (semantic divergence metric): > 0.07 absolute shift => FLAG for human review

Fallback strategies:
- Immediate hot rollback: revert routing to previous model variant (automated via rollout API).
- Soft-fallback: route only new requests to fallback variant for 10% of incoming user queries, hold rest. Allows canary to stay but reduces impact.
- Graceful degrade path: switch to cached responses for deterministic endpoints where acceptable.

Observability checklist (minimum dashboards/alerts):
- Token-level cost (per route/model)
- Latency heatmap by model and sequence-length bucket
- Error waterfall (5xx, timeout, OOM) by slice
- Semantic divergence histogram across prompt-eval set
- Top-20 user-facing failure examples stream (for steward review)
- Canary-specific PagerDuty routing for immediate steward notification

Experiment & A/B pairing guidance:
- For A/B (feature gating) pair with canary by isolating A/B within a canary slice to safeguard larger population. Example: 5% pilot split A/B into 2.5%/2.5% for rapid comparison.
- Use offline randomized holdout for heavy instrumentation to avoid observational bias (persist assignment keys).
- When running multi-model A/B, ensure per-cohort telemetry is aggregated to disentangle traffic noise.

Synthetic traffic recipes (quick):
- Low-latency probe: 500 requests/min, sequence length 16-64, mix of short/medium templates
- Long-context probe: 200 requests over 2h with sequences 1024-2048 tokens (if supported)
- Edge-case probe: 1000 adversarial prompts from evaluation set (safety / hallucination focus)

Simulation notes (useful for preflight):
- Run local rollout-sim with 10k traces generated from real traffic traces (anonymized). Observe queue build-ups and tail latency under synthetic spikes.
- Simulate partial KV-cache warmup: cold-start can show short-lived p99 spikes; expect decoupling to reveal whether p99 regressions are model-side or infra-side.

Runbook snippets (quick commands / ops actions):
- Pause ramp: console rollout pause <release-id> --reason "p99 spike"
- Rollback to variant: console rollout revert <release-id> --variant previous --force
- Snapshot telemetry for snapshot-id: console telemetry snapshot --slice <id> --since 2h

Post-release:
- 72h check-in: steward + eval lead meet, summarize top-5 regressions / unexpected behaviors.
- 3 business day retro: includes root cause, signal adjustments, test case additions to eval harness. Add newly-found failure prompts to blocked-prompt list.

Open questions / tradeoffs we need decisions on:
- How aggressive should automatic rollback thresholds be for high-volume endpoints (tradeoff speed vs noise)?
- Default ramp timings: is 12h per step enough for overnight global regions? Suggest region-aware ramp times.
- Does the console UI need a dedicated microrelease mode (preset gates + steward handoff) or use templates?

Next steps (action items):
- Miguel: prototype microrelease preset in console (ETA 3w) -> github PR link above.
- Karen: curate 200-case eval probe set for pilot cohorts (ETA 2w).
- Samir: add synthetic traffic recipes to rollout-sim and run 3 scenario sims (ETA 1w).
- Asha (owner): schedule cross-team dry run in staging (target week of 2024-11-11).

Quick checklist before scheduling pilot:
- [ ] Eval harness green (all blocking tests pass)
- [ ] Synthetic dry canary run (2h) results saved
- [ ] Steward assigned and PD rota updated
- [ ] Rollout preset created in console with pause guardrails
- [ ] Communication to affected product/platform stakeholders

Notes / brainstorming fragments (scratchpad):
- Consider a "stitching" concept: when model and routing must change together, create a two-phase release where small routing opt-in exposes new model only for warmed sessions.
- Could we include a lightweight divergence sentinel that automatically samples and computes BLEU/semantic-similarity on a small rolling window? Might help detect silent drift.
- Idea: microrelease labels in telemetry to allow cohort-level budgeting/cost attribution (helps product decide continuation).

End of draft.

(Internal: this is a working doc — keep edits quick and mark TODOs inline. Related: CONFLUENCE-ROLL-ORCH-42 for long-form policy doc.)
